title: lint_handoffs.py reports 263 BLOCKER + 195 MAJOR + 1 MINOR across historical handoffs (2269 checked) -- large pre-existing bookkeeping debt, not caused by this run
symptom: Running `python3 tools/lint_handoffs.py` (mandatory pre-completion check per CLAUDE.md's Bookkeeping Is Not Optional directive) at the end of WF03-GH495-20260808's Step Final reports 263 BLOCKER, 195 MAJOR, and 1 MINOR findings across 2269 handoffs checked. None of the findings reference this run's own handoff files (handoffs/WF03-GH495-20260808/*) -- confirmed by grep. All findings carry timestamps from historical runs spanning 2026-05-22 through 2026-08-07 (WF01-*, WF02-*, WF03-*, ADHOC-* prefixes). Categories observed: H001 (11+ handoff files with unparseable JSON -- trailing commas, invalid control characters, wrong encoding), H002 (8 files in WF02-iss105-token-model-schema-20260611 where `result` is a JSON string instead of an object, which breaks any h['result']['status'] lookup), H003 (dozens of files where completed_at precedes started_at, i.e. inverted/local-time-labelled-UTC timestamps), H009 (~20 files where a PENDING/IN_PROGRESS step has later COMPLETED steps in the same run -- the pipeline advanced past a step it never formally closed), H010 (registry.json is missing 82.3% of all historical handoffs from its index).
root_cause:
Consistent with the pattern CLAUDE.md's own Bookkeeping section already documents (2026-08-05 pipeline audit: 'directives about recording the work were not [followed]' -- log append rate 44%->0.4%, registry coverage 3.4%, timestamp validity 8.6%). This finding is a fresh quantification of that same long-standing gap via the tool that was built to detect it, not a new defect class.

TRIAGE (WF03-GH594-20260808 Step 1, ISSUE-FIXER, 2026-08-08): re-ran lint_handoffs.py against 2270 handoffs -- 263 BLOCKER + 195 MAJOR + 1 MINOR, broken out by check code as: H003 148, H008 88, H007 69, H013 53, H009 38, H004 34, H001 11, H002 9, H005 5, H006 3, H010 1. Sample-verified 2-3 real files per category (not just the tool's summary text) against tools/lint_handoffs.py's actual check logic:
  - H002 (9 files, all in WF02-iss105-token-model-schema-20260611): result field is a JSON-string-encoded object; json.loads(result_string) round-trips cleanly to the exact expected shape (verified). SAFE, purely additive/deterministic -- no data invented.
  - H008 (88 files): UTF-8 BOM prefix; stripping it is a pure byte-level operation, content unchanged. SAFE.
  - H010 (1 finding, 1868/2270 files missing from registry.json): each missing handoff carries its own created_at/status in its own file; reconciliation only ADDS registry entries sourced from each handoff's own recorded fields, never invents data. SAFE.
  - H001 (11 files): mixed failure modes on inspection -- ~7 are PowerShell curly-quote/cp1252-encoding corruption (mechanically recoverable via decode-fallback + verify-round-trip-before-write, confirmed cp1252 decode succeeds on WF02-lua06-16-20260528/step-02-backend-dev.json), but the remainder are genuine structural typos (e.g. ADHOC-gh402-db-cleanup-hang-20260803/step-00-backend-dev-db-cleanup.json line 46 closes an object with ']' instead of '}') requiring per-file judgment about which delimiter was intended. NEEDS CODE-DESIGNER TO SPECIFY a verify-before-write repair (accept a fix only if the repaired file re-parses AND a byte-diff shows only the targeted corrupted characters changed) -- do not blind-script the structural subset.
  - H006 (3 files): 'FAILED'->'FAIL' and 'PARTIAL_PASS'->'PARTIAL' are unambiguous renames; 'CONDITIONAL' has no 1:1 mapping and needs the file's own context read by hand.
  - H003/H004/H005/H009/H013/H007 (148/34/5/38/53/69 findings): confirmed NOT safely fixable this run -- see docs/issues/ISS-0627.json (GH #596) for full per-category reasoning. In short: H003/H004/H005/H009 have no recoverable source for the true value anywhere in the file (any fix is fabrication); H013's offset is computable but its causal timezone is not recorded in the file; H007 is an early alternate schema (workflow_id/sequence vs run_id/step) requiring an explicit migration decision, not a silent key-add.
acceptance_criteria: SCOPE NARROWED by triage to the safe-mechanical subset only: H002 (9 files, unwrap JSON-string result into object), H008 (88 files, strip UTF-8 BOM), H010 (1868 missing registry entries, additive reconciliation from each handoff's own recorded fields)

CODE-DESIGNER produces a design for a single repair script covering H002+H008+H010, plus a verify-before-write repair approach for the H001 encoding-corruption subset (~7 of 11 files) distinct from its structural-typo subset
H006's 2 unambiguous renames (FAILED->FAIL, PARTIAL_PASS->PARTIAL) may be folded into the same script; the CONDITIONAL case is excluded (see ISS-0627)
Re-run lint_handoffs.py after remediation and confirm H002/H008/H010 counts reach 0 and H006 drops from 3 to 1

All remaining categories (H001-structural, H003, H004, H005, H006-CONDITIONAL, H007, H009, H013 -- 292 of 458 findings) are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this issue, split to docs/issues/ISS-0627.json / GH #596 for case-by-case handling or permanent acknowledgment, per CLAUDE.md's 'a wrong-guess fix to an audit trail is worse than an honestly-flagged gap' principle
notes:
Discovered incidentally while completing WF03-GH495-20260808's Step Final (DOC-UPDATER), which runs lint_handoffs.py as a mandatory pre-completion check. This run's own handoff files are clean (0 findings), so the finding did not block this run's completion -- filed and forwarded per CLAUDE.md's Unblock-Everything / No-Issue-Left-Local-Only directives rather than fixed in-scope, since remediating ~8 months of cross-run bookkeeping debt is a distinct, large body of work unrelated to ISS-0169's Lua limiter wiring.
